Source. The attacker-controlled main entity is materialized as a memory-backed parser input. For this witness the entity length is 197 bytes and the harness has already reduced the raw fuzz budget `35649` to `maxAlloc == 37` before entering libxml2.
The first four entity bytes `00 00 00 3c` are interpreted as UCS-4BE, creating the decoding state that turns the witness into a document beginning with `<` instead of a raw NUL-prefixed byte stream.
The parser switches the memory input to the detected UCS-4BE decoder, so `xmlParseDocument` later reaches the start-tag path and calls `xmlParseElement(ctxt)` on decoded document content.
On the crashing QName path, the complex NCName parser snapshots the current offset within the live parser buffer. This offset is later recombined with `BASE_PTR` at dictionary lookup time.
Because lookahead falls below `INPUT_CHUNK`, character decoding requests more bytes from the same parser input during NCName parsing.
Under the witness's `maxAlloc == 37` malloc-failure budget, this refill path fails, so the buffered parser input enters an out-of-memory error state before the QName parse has finished.

Root-cause step. After the refill failure leaves `buf->error` set, vulnerable input-update logic truncates the parser input to the global empty-string literal instead of preserving the old buffer and offsets. The upstream fix removes this truncation behavior.

The QName parser uses the previously captured offset together with the now-truncated `BASE_PTR`. That transforms an offset into the real parser buffer into a pointer into the global empty-string object while still forwarding a positive maximum length to dictionary lookup.
Dictionary lookup trusts the corrupted name pointer from step 8 and uses the supplied NCName length as the hash loop bound.
Sink. The hash loop dereferences bytes from the global empty-string literal as if it were a real NCName buffer. ASan records the first invalid read immediately past that 1-byte object.
